summary: Interpreted the immediate-demotion receipt (CheckRun 023f240cad604dd7874ba0054537bc81, exit 0). All six comparisons hold: the two caught-up runs and the added immediate-demotion case all converged within 0-20ms, every node ended at the configuration index, and no node's view was stale once its log held the entry. The baseline events explain why the immediate variant did not differ: with the bootstrapped leader campaigning only after ten to twenty seconds, followers already had the configuration and no-op (LastIndex 2) before the leader was observed, so both constructions coincide. The question's suspicion is therefore refuted across both constructions - a committed voter-to-non-voter transition is reflected by every peer within about one sample interval - and the isolated near_node_self_voter field from the extended-window harness is retained as an unexplained artefact that cannot affect the VerifyLeader result, since that result is decided by the leader's own configuration (voters 3, nonvoters 1, quorum 2) and by which acknowledgements the leader can obtain with the far voters unreachable. Limits are stated (healthy unloaded cluster only, seven runs total at 20ms sampling, an immediate construction that did not actually precede adoption, configuration index read from the leader). Using the remaining allocation to check one concrete producer/consumer relationship on the VerifyLeader line rather than restating this account.
